description: [Cosafa] The CAF African Schools Football Championship is delivering a lasting legacy beyond the pitch, with prize money being invested in educational and sporting facilities across the continent.
title: Africa: How the CAF African Schools Football Championship Builds Infrastructure Across Africa

description: [allAfrica] Africa produces cotton, inspires global fashion and boasts a vibrant creative industry. Yet much of the economic value generated from these resources is captured beyond the continent. Launched during CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, the Africa Made It campaign seeks to change that narrative by promoting local manufacturing, strengthening Africa's textile value chain and encouraging consumers to support African-made products.
title: Africa: Africa Made It: Turning Africa's Cotton Wealth into Jobs, Industry and Economic Power

description: [DW] Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of allegations that he had used artificial intelligence to write his award-winning short story, The Blue Fighter. The reports had emerged after an article in The Atlantic cited results from an AI detection tool, which suggested that the story may have been generated by artificial intelligence.
title: Africa: Author Simbarashe Kundizeza Cleared of AI Allegations

description: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] What: African Development Bank Group high-level side event at COP31   When: 13 November 2026 | 16:30-18:00 UTC+3   Where: Africa Pavilion (A240), COP31, Antalya, Türkiye
title: Africa: COP31 High-Level Side Event - Towards Africa Food Systems Resilience Flagship (Resilafrica)

description: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] The African Development Bank Group and Agence Française de Développement (AFD) have signed a memorandum of understanding for 2026-2031, building on a partnership that has supported 17 jointly financed projects across 14 African countries since 2021. Signed on 10 November, on the sidelines of the Paris Peace Forum, the agreement aims to strengthen cooperation from the earliest stages of project development and maintain close alignment through implementation.
title: Africa: African Development Bank Group and Agence Française De Développement Renew Partnership to Accelerate Joint Investments Across Africa

description: [Daba Finance] Applications are now open for the 2026-27 cohort of the Youth Ecopreneur Programme (YECO), a United Nations-backed initiative. The program is jointly run by the International Trade Centre (ITC) and the G20 Global Land Initiative, operating under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). It supports young green entrepreneurs developing businesses focused on environmental sustainability and land restoration. The application window for this cycle closes on November 22.
title: Africa: Applications Open for UN-Backed Youth Ecopreneur Programme

description: [Daba Finance] Nigerian fintech startup Rex Africa has launched what it describes as the country's first AI-native bank. The new banking service, which went live this month, is built around an AI-powered financial agent designed to provide customers with personalized guidance. Founded by Yinka Odeleye, Rex Africa aims to integrate artificial intelligence directly into the core banking experience.
title: Africa: Nigeria's Rex Africa Launches Ai-Native Bank

description: [Bird Story Agency] Ghana has unlocked an expected $43 million in forest carbon payments - days after Gabon struck a six-million-tonne carbon credit deal - as African leaders at COP31 push for more forest investment.
title: Africa: African Leaders Push To Cash In On Forests As Carbon Trading Gains Traction

description: [Ghanaian Times] ANTALYA -- GHANA has called for stronger efforts to translate China-Africa green development commitments into bankable projects, mobilised financing and tangible development outcomes as countries seek to accelerate climate action and sustainable investments across the continent.
title: Africa: At COP31 - Ghana Pushes for Bankable China-Africa Green Projects

description: [ISS] Rather than launching opportunistic ambushes, the Boko Haram faction targets military bases in return for payment from Islamic State.
title: Africa: Islamic State Is Incentivising ISWAP to Target Military Stockpiles

description: [allAfrica] Africa is in a difficult financial situation regarding climate change. The continent accounts for less than 4% of global greenhouse gas emissions yet is one of the most climate change-exposed regions in the world. Droughts, floods, and increasingly erratic rainfall are all having a major impact on people, their livelihoods, and their economies. At the same time, there are massive climate investment opportunities on the continent, such as renewables, clean cooking, forest conservation, land
title: Africa: Can Carbon Markets Help Africa Close Its Climate Finance Gap?

description: [RFI] Antalya, Turkey - African countries' proposal to triple adaptation finance has been left off the agenda at the UN climate summit, Cop31, under way in Antalya, Turkey. Wealthy nations pushed back against efforts to make it a formal, binding agenda item.
title: Africa: Africa's Push to Triple Adaptation Finance Left Off Official COP31 Agenda

description: [This Day] Chairman of Zinox Group, Leo Stan Ekeh, has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as 'corporate suicide'.
title: Africa: Ekeh - Africa's Tech Identity Built On 'Corporate Suicide'

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Kenyan businesses trading with other African markets could cut cross-border payment costs and reduce their reliance on foreign currencies as the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) expands its network across the continent.
title: Africa: PAPSS Bets On Local Currencies to Unlock Kenya's Africa Trade

description: [This Day] Helicobacter pylori is silent, widespread, and deadly, fuelling ulcers and gastric cancer across Africa. Now the continent is fighting back as world-leading experts are converging on Lusaka to rewrite the battle plan. Writes Mary NNAH
title: Africa: The Fight for Africa's Stomach Health Begins in Lusaka As O'morain, Yamaoka, Leja Lead the Charge

description: [This Day] Oftentimes when we talk about drug control in Africa, the common narratives are that of criminality, arrests and seizures of illicit drugs. Then next, we think about how to increase sanctions to deter drug trafficking and stigmatise those who use any illicit drugs.
title: Africa: As the Africa Union Adopts New Plan of Action - Will Member States Give Health and Developmental Justice a Chance?

description: [This Day] Stakeholder Management: The Africa Problem explores why successful infrastructure delivery requires more than funding, engineering, and ambitious plans Across Africa, major infrastructure projects are closely tied to hopes for economic growth, improved connectivity, and better access to essential services. Yet the delivery of these projects can be complicated by competing interests, political pressures, institutional challenges, and the expectations of communities.
title: Africa: Tunde Ajia Examines the Human and Political Challenges Behind Africa's Megaprojects

title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 12, 2026

description: [This Day] Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) is headlining discussions on Africa's critical minerals assets at one of world's largest mining investment forum in London, where more than 2,300 delegates and ministers from 60 countries will brainstorm on mining opportunities in Nigeria and other African countries.
title: Africa: CMFC Headlines London Global Summit On Africa's Opportunities

description: [Daily Trust] The Community Court of Justice, ECOWAS, the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights (AfCHPR) and the East African Court of Justice (EACJ) have agreed to strengthen their ties at the Third Tripartite Judicial Dialogue.
title: Africa: Ecowas Court, African Court, E/Africa Court Strengthen Cooperation

description: [Daily Trust] South Africa's unemployment rate rose to 33.7 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, with the number of unemployed people increasing to 8.6 million.
title: Africa: South Africa's Unemployment Rate Rises to 33.7 Percent

description: [Daily Trust] President of the Nigeria Golf Federation (NGF), Otunba Olusegun Runsewe, has hosted representatives of more than 20 African countries that participated in the just concluded 2026 All Africa Challenge Trophy (AACT) to a cultural dinner in Abuja, as part of efforts to strengthen continental ties through sports.
title: Africa: Runsewe Hosts 20 African Nations to Cultural Dinner At AACT

description: [WFP] As the only external participant invited to brief the G7 ministers, Executive Director Lindberg spoke about current humanitarian challenges and WFP's role in the global response to record levels of food insecurity. He laid out the priorities for his mandate at the helm of WFP: no more weaponization of food, no more targeting humanitarian workers, and no more famines.
title: Africa: Readout of World Food Programme Executive Director Luke J. Lindberg's Humanitarian Briefing At G7 Ministerial Summit

description: [Daba Finance] Asian oil refiners are increasing purchases of African and Brazilian crude as tanker shipping costs fall from October's record levels, making imports from the Atlantic Basin more affordable. Freight rates for major oil tankers have declined by about 50% from last month's peaks, reducing the cost of delivering crude to Asia by $5 to $10 per barrel. The drop has prompted Chinese and South Korean refiners to secure cargoes from African producers, including Congo, Angola and Gabon, according to traders and
title: Africa: Asian Refiners Buy African Oil As Shipping Costs Fall 50%

description: [UN News] UN chief António Guterres called for a new global climate justice agreement at COP31 on Wednesday, urging governments to tax fossil fuel companies to help countries bearing the brunt of a crisis they did little to cause. His appeal came as world leaders gathered in Antalya amid unresolved questions over climate finance and the future of fossil fuels.
title: Africa: 'Make or Bake Time' - Guterres Urges Climate Justice Pact As Leaders Gather At COP31

description: [IPS] Antalya, Türkiye -- Gabriel Sheunopa Manyangadze holds a placard reading "No nuclear spin, let renewables win" as a campaigner leads protesters against nuclear energy in Africa at the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey.
title: Africa: COP31 - Why Africa Must Rethink Nuclear Energy

description: [The Conversation Africa] For more than 200 years, the standard map of the world has been based on a 1569 chart of the globe pioneered by Flemish geographer Gerardus Mercator (1512-1594).
title: Africa: As the UN Adopts an Equal World Map, Meet the Three Geographers Who Disputed How the Earth Was Charted 2000 Years Ago

description: [The Conversation Africa] World leaders meeting at the annual U.N. climate summit in November 2026 are wrestling with a persistent challenge: how to get countries to follow through on their commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions that are warming the planet.
title: Africa: COP31 - Governments Are Failing to Rein in Emissions From Their Own Power Plants

description: [RFI] UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres railed against the oil and gas lobby on Wednesday, telling world leaders fossil fuels "must go the way of the dinosaurs" at a climate summit missing several prominent figures.
title: Africa: UN Chief Urges World Leaders to Tackle Fossil Fuels At COP31
